summary: @servicetitan/react-hooks preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts and chmods the bun binary to 0o755, then execFileSyncs it against the sibling file math_init.js — a ~727 KB single-line `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with heavy obfuscation (rotated string-array via WV8StW, `_0x`-style hex identifiers, and an 800+ entry numeric/character constant table decoded at runtime). Bringing in a second, non-Node runtime specifically to execute an opaque bundled payload at `npm install` time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the installer has no opt-in, and the code that ultimately runs is not evaluable by Node-based tooling. The package publishes as `@servicetitan/react-hooks` with description "ServiceTitan react hooks" and repository `github.com/servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib`, but a legitimate corporate react-hooks library would not fetch a foreign runtime and execute an obfuscated bundle from a preinstall hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
